prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the claims-triage agent (home and motor claims assessment within delegated authority) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: worried the house is in a flood zone. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 2)
response: {"items":[{"type":"fact","content":"When a member says they are worried the house is in a flood zone, I check the location first against the postcode and any nearby watercourse or coastal indicators before assuming the risk is high."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the worry is based on a recent storm or local news, the concern is often greater than the actual flood exposure, so I separate perception from the property’s known flood history."},{"type":"fact","content":"When there has been a past flood claim, I look at whether it was river, surface water or blocked drainage, because the type of flooding changes both the assessment and the likely future risk."},{"type":"preference","content":"When evidence is limited, I prefer clear, practical questions about where water entered, how deep it got and whether neighbouring homes were affected, rather than broad questions that invite guesswork."},{"type":"fact","content":"When a property is near a river or low-lying land, I check whether any flood warnings or alerts have been issued recently, as this helps me distinguish a general fear from an active exposure."},{"type":"observation","content":"When members mention flooded roads or standing water locally, it does not always mean the home itself is in a flood zone, so I treat access flooding and property flooding as separate issues."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the home has modern drainage, raised thresholds or previous flood resilience work, I note these features because they can reduce the practical severity even if the area has some exposure."},{"type":"preference","content":"When I am unsure whether the risk is material, I prefer to document the concern plainly and escalate with the evidence attached, rather than dismissing the worry without a clear basis."},{"type":"fact","content":"When a member asks about flood zone status, I explain that a postcode alone is not enough for a final decision, and that local topography, drainage and nearby watercourses all matter."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the claim is otherwise straightforward, a flood-zone concern should not delay triage unnecessarily, because many properties with some exposure still have no current flooding issue."}]}
